#4606. Tech Report: 5 ways to make sure your console isn't holding back your GTA 6 performance

📅 27 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1606 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Engadget ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: 5 ways to make sure your console isn't holding back your GTA 6 performance

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1606 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • GTA 6 already pushes every PS5 and Xbox to its limit, but is yours falling short of it?
  • Within days of GTA 6's November 19 debut, Xbox owners had found a way to break its 30 fps cap.
  • It's fundamentally the processor that's holding GTA 6 at 30 fps on current-gen consoles (PS5 Pro included).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6 already pushes every PS5 and Xbox to its limit, but is yours falling short of it?

Within days of GTA 6's November 19 debut, Xbox owners had found a way to break its 30 fps cap. The trick, which was first reported on November 22, involves flipping a Series X's output between 60Hz and 120Hz, then hopping in and out of the game using Quick Resume. It works... sort of. When Digital Foundry tested the trick, it found the uncapped Series X averaged about 36 fps over an hour of play. The game's cars and animations also moved noticeably faster than they're meant to (some at around double speed).

It's fundamentally the processor that's holding GTA 6 at 30 fps on current-gen consoles (PS5 Pro included). The fact that a Series X with the limiter switched off is only able to find six extra frames per second illustrates how little is left to play with, so tinkering with settings isn't going to do very much. What you can do, however, is check whether your console is making the most of its available hardware.

A system that's out of date, stuck in a stale session, choked with dust or reading the game off the wrong drive could easily fall short. Here's how to find out if yours is falling victim to any of these problems.

I've played around 60 hours of GTA 6 in the last week on an original-model PS5 I bought in 2021, and haven't seen too much dipping below 30 fps outside of full-on rampages. There are some drops, though, which aligns with others' findings that it regularly falls slightly under 30 fps during ordinary city drives, and dropped to 23 fps during a grenade launcher test with multiple explosions. The PS5 Pro fares much better, with stress tests finding that it maintains 30 fps for the most part, only dropping to around 24 fps when the player wrecks as many cars as possible all at once.

It has been revealed that the Series X, meanwhile, generally holds its 30 fps target but can slip during busy scenes and explosions. The Series S, which renders at 720p internally, struggles quite a bit. It hovers between 25 and 30 fps for most of the game and drops to as low as 20 in busy areas and when vehicles start blowing up, with one explosive scene briefly tanking it to 18 or 19 fps during Kotaku's testing.

Industry observers note that since consoles don't have built-in frame rate counters, the simplest way to monitor fps is to watch for stuttering. If the action gets choppy during firefights, police chases, explosions and pile-ups, your frame rate is dropping, which is somewhat normal for current-gen console hardware. You shouldn't be losing frames during cutscenes or when walking or driving around normally, even on a Series S.

Industry observers note that if you are, that's a sign something else is amiss with your console. As for native 40 or 60 fps modes, Rockstar's technology production director Marc Chambers has stated that even the PS5 Pro's processor isn't powerful enough, settling a major question about GTA 6's controversial FPS decision.

According to recent reports, rockstar released GTA 6's first post-launch upgrade on November 23. The patch notes describe fixes for several concerns that caused the game to crash, along with bugs that could stall playthroughs, from broken autosaves to story phone calls that wouldn't come through. Nowhere in the patch notes is frame rate or performance mentioned, though. The rumor mill started spinning up shortly after, claiming that Rockstar would push a stuttering fix on November 25, but nothing came of it.

To check whether your game is up to date on PS5, highlight GTA 6 on the main menu, press the Options button on your controller and select Check for Revision. Xbox players should go to My games & apps, choose Manage and then check under Updates to see titles that have newer versions available. Storage might be an matter, given the base game's absolutely massive 212GB size. Sony has warned that installing data can require roughly twice as much free space as the install size, so a console that's filled to the brim might refuse to install the patch.

Players were still posting about error CE-108255-1 and others as recently as November 25. Sony describes it, rather vaguely, as an error with a game or application. If it keeps happening after updating, Sony's crash troubleshooting runs through installing the latest system software, starting a newly introduced save and, as a last resort, deleting and reinstalling the game.

According to recent reports, quick Resume on the Xbox Series X and S saves the state of a game when you switch to another one, then reloads that state when you come back. It's the feature that enables the frame rate glitch mentioned earlier. It works by setting the console to 60Hz, starting GTA 6, switching to 120Hz on the loading screen, launching a different game and then jumping back in through Quick Resume. This relaunches the game with its cap removed, allowing it to run faster than it's meant to — though it can lead to crashes and bugs.

Industry observers note that in testing by Digital Foundry, the uncapped Series X only reached 60 fps when flying a plane with nothing but sky in view. It managed around 40 fps on highways with light traffic, but barely beat 30 in heavier scenes, such as busy streets. It concluded that 60 fps is simply out of reach on current hardware and that although a 40 fps mode with VRR could make sense on Series X, it wouldn't be a clear improvement over the current 30 fps cap.

Sources indicate that to get a clean start on Xbox, press the Xbox button, highlight GTA 6, press the Menu button and then select Quit. You can also manually choose which games use Quick Resume through Manage game and add-ons > Quick Resume settings on a game's tile. Microsoft added that feature back in April because Quick Resume doesn't always behave as intended in certain titles (particularly after a game has been inactive for a while).

The PS5, meanwhile, keeps games suspended in rest mode. Thus, closing GTA 6 by highlighting its icon on the main menu, pressing Options and choosing Close Game, or turning the console off completely, achieves the same result. Be sure to save your game regularly since you won't have sleep mode as a fallback.

In a recent development, sony's PS5 safety guide recommends keeping your console roughly 4 inches away from walls, out of closed cabinets or other cramped spaces, and off long-pile carpets. It should also be free of dust on its vents. Microsoft recommends similar for the Xbox: a well-ventilated, relatively cool spot away from heat sources, with nothing sitting on, under or right next to the console. Since both went on sale in late 2020, plenty of consoles have had six years to suck up dust.

While neither Sony nor Microsoft says that a hot console will lead to slower gameplay, heat stress wears components down more promptly. Also, if your PS5 gets too hot, you'll be met with an on-screen warning, at which point Sony recommends switching it off and letting it cool down to prevent damage. On Xbox, meanwhile, poor ventilation and/or overheating is one of two causes Microsoft gives for the console switching itself off without warning. So while a hot console won't necessarily cut the frame rate, it could crash your game or force your console to shut down.

There's also been speculation that overheating could be behind some of the PS5 crashes we've seen since GTA 6's launch. That's possibly because of degradation of the liquid metal that sits between the processor and its cooler. A clean console isn't a workaround for hardware limitations and faults, but it does remove heat as a potential suspect.

Recent findings suggest that sony indicates that before cleaning your PS5, you should unplug it and wipe the outside with a soft, dry cloth. Its side covers come off, allowing you to clean the dust catchers more easily.

GTA 6 needs up to 212GB of free space on both consoles, which is close to a third of the roughly 667GB that's usable on an 825GB PS5. That might push you toward installing the game on a secondary M.2 SSD added to the console's expansion slot. While the PS5 is compatible with a wide range of PCIe Gen4 drives, Sony recommends a sequential read speed of 5,500 MB/s or faster and requires a heatsink or similar cooling. But even with a compatible drive faster than that, games won't necessarily perform the same as they would on the internal SSD.

As you'd expect from such a dense title, the game is constantly pulling in data as you move around Leonida. Digital Foundry's Series S testing found frame rate drops in situations that put a heavy load on the console's AI or streaming, so the game leans on its storage more than others do.

While we haven't seen any examples of GTA 6 behaving problematically when installed on an M.2 drive, if you're doing so and experience stutter when you shouldn't, moving the game back to internal storage is worth a try. On your PS5, go to Settings > Storage > M.2 SSD Storage > Move Games and Apps to move as needed. On an Xbox, Series X and S games can only run from the internal SSD or Microsoft's Storage Expansion Card, which Microsoft says performs identically to the internal drive.

Apple Stays Winning as Smartphone Sales Continue to Slump

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • RAM prices are continuing to put the squeeze on smartphone sales, and even people who typically buy less expensive phones appear to be holding off on upgrading.
  • According to recent reports, according to a upcoming report from Counterpoint Research, smartphone sales in the third quarter of 2026 fell by 9% compared to the same period in 2025.
  • In a recent development, in terms of market share, Samsung held steady at around 25%, while Motorola, Google and other companies saw their slice of the pie decline.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

RAM prices are continuing to put the squeeze on smartphone sales, and even people who typically buy less expensive phones appear to be holding off on upgrading.

According to recent reports, according to a upcoming report from Counterpoint Research, smartphone sales in the third quarter of 2026 fell by 9% compared to the same period in 2025. The report attributed the drop to rising memory costs, which are hurting sales at the low end of the Android phone market.

In a recent development, in terms of market share, Samsung held steady at around 25%, while Motorola, Google and other companies saw their slice of the pie decline. Where did those sales go, you might be wondering? Unsurprisingly, Apple’s broad range of iPhone models — from the 17E to its newest foldable flagship, the $1,999 iPhone Duo — bumped the tech giant’s share of the smartphone market from 50% to 57% since last year.

Smartphone-makers with cheaper phone lineups suffered due to component costs, particularly memory, eating into their margins. “There, OEMs have little room to absorb a higher bill of materials without raising prices or cutting volume,” noted Counterpoint Senior Analyst Emily Herbert.

It has been revealed that the slowdown in phone sales has been happening all year. In the last quarter, the market slumped by 20%, more than was expected at the time. The build-out of data centers to support the ever-expanding AI industry has led to shortages of memory components. In turn, the prices of those components have spiked, raising prices of not just smartphones, but game consoles, PCs and other electronics.

Read more: Best Black Friday iPhone Deals.

In a recent development, black Friday, Cyber Monday and the Christmas gift-giving season typically mean strong phone sales for companies like Apple and Samsung. But the memory component crisis isn’t going to go away that swiftly, and prices of phones are still higher overall.

Counterpoint predicts that smartphone sales will remain weak in the next quarter and that US carriers may be more selective about the promotions they offer this year. AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon are also seeing declining sales and customers are getting choosier about committing to phones that often cost more than $1,000. People are also looking to second-hand and refurbished phones instead of buying newly introduced.

It has been revealed that “Consumers are timing their purchases around the best deals more than ever, if they buy at all,” mentioned Counterpoint Senior Analyst Maurice Klaehne. “This year’s holiday sales cycle will look quite different from usual.”.

If you're looking for a robot vacuum and mop combo that won't break the bank, the Roborock Q10 S5+ is on sale for $229.99, down from $549.99. That's a 58% discount, or $320 in savings.

Mashable's former robot vacuum expert, Leah Stodart, notes it's one of the quietest robot vacuums she's ever tested. It also has 10,000 Pa of suction, obstacle avoidance, and a sonic mop that scrubs (instead of just dragging a damp pad around). The mop lifts automatically when it detects carpet, and the self-emptying dock holds up to 70 days' worth of dust.

Right now, you can get the Roborock Qrevo Curv 2 Flow for $549.99, down from $999.99. That's a 45% discount, or a $450 price cut, on a top-rated 2026 model.

Stodart named it the "Best Roller Mop Robot Vacuum under $1,000." Its petite dock makes it a great option for people who are "limited on floor space," and it cleans with precision. "The Curv 2 Flow's obstacle avoidance is some of the best I've ever experienced," writes Stodart. It delivers 20,000 Pa of suction, has a Dual Zero-Tangle System, plus a full-service dock that empties the dust bin and washes and dries the roller mop.

Upgrading your whole setup at once usually gets pricey fast, which makes this deal worth a look for Black Friday. Through Nov. 30, Amazon is taking 20% off a six-pack of the X-Sense SC07-W Wireless Interconnected Smoke and Carbon Monoxide Detector, dropping it from $269.99 down to $215.99.

GameStop — Online orders are off; you will have to walk into a store to find one.

The remake rebuilds the 1998 classic from the ground up with modernized controls, a fully orchestrated soundtrack, reworked dungeon puzzles, and expanded Hyrule environments. Since the $520 console doesn’t include the game, everyone is rushing to lock down a system before launch day.

According to recent reports, black Friday deals are coming in hot and heavy. We're inundated with fresh price drops on laptops, headphones, fitness trackers, and everything in between. And yes, we're seeing a huge number of price drops on Apple.

According to recent reports, wading through the deals on iPads, MacBooks, and AirPods, it's tough to ignore T-Mobile's massive sale on iPhones. If you've been waiting until now to upgrade, you're in luck: For limited-time, the Apple iPhone 18 Pro is free at T-Mobile. Yes, you read that right.

T-Mobile keeps things surprisingly flexible when it comes to qualifying for this Black Friday deal. You can port your existing phone number from an eligible rival carrier to a qualifying T-Mix proposal, and T-Mobile covers the full cost of the phone. Alternatively, existing customers can trade in an eligible phone in any condition on a qualifying T-Mix plan.

T-Mobile distributes the full discount as 36 monthly bill credits. If you leave T-Mobile or cancel your line before that three-year payment blueprint ends, the credits stop immediately, and you will owe the remaining balance on the device.

You are also still required to pay local sales tax on the phone's full $1,199 retail value upfront, plus T-Mobile's standard $35 device connection fee per line at checkout. Unfortunately, you can't escape those upfront charges.

Score the Apple iPhone 18 Pro for free with T-Mobile over Black Friday.

Why not take a break from your uncle’s MAGA monolog, put down your turkey-laden fork, and embrace a more modern American Thanksgiving tradition: shopping for the best Black Friday deals. This weekend used to be about retailers dumping old stock at substantial discounts to make room for the new, but now the deals on tech come thick and fast, often on the latest gear (though it’s not always clear which discounts are real).

In a recent development, welcome to WIRED’s guide to the best Black Friday tech deals. I can promise you that everything here is worth buying (we’ve tested and recommended all of it), and these are real discounts (not the year-round price). If you need an upgrade, a pick-me-up, or some great techy gifts, you’re in the right place. For more Black Friday deals, check out our other guides, like the Best Black Friday TV Deals or the Best Black Friday Mattress Deals.

Perhaps the most exciting release of the year (unless you're an Apple person), the Z Fold8 is our top pick of the best folding phones. Samsung’s experience shows with a fresh form factor that feels revelatory. Both the 5.5-inch cover screen and the 7.7-inch inner screen are bright, sharp, and genuinely useful. There's a Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 chipset and plenty of stamina, thanks to the 4,800-mAh silicon-carbon battery. A $350 discount brings it to the lowest price we’ve seen yet.

After testing many, many Apple 3-in-1 wireless chargers, this is the one that claimed a permanent place on my bedside table. It looks classy, and I love the weighted base, enabling you to grab your iPhone without pulling the whole charger off the nightstand. The pad also tilts and holds your iPhone vertically or horizontally, with support for StandBy mode. It can fast-charge capable iPhone and Apple Watch models and charge any AirPods with a wireless charging case. The 5-foot braided cable is permanently attached, and there’s a 36-watt wall charger in the box.

Handy as they are for keeping you connected when your phone dies unexpectedly, portable chargers can be very same-y. One of the reasons the Nimble Champ is in our Best Power Banks guide is Nimble’s focus on the environment. It’s made from 90 percent certified recycled plastic and comes in fully biodegradable packaging. It also works well, with capacities starting from 5,200 mAh, with USB-A and USB-C ports, and up to 15-watt charging.

According to recent reports, while it's no longer my top pick of the best travel adapters, this is still a solid option and will keep all of your gadgetry running wherever you travel. There's a classic slider design for the plug that covers more than 200 countries, but you also get one USB-C port, two USB-A ports, and a handy retractable USB-C cable (perfect if you're forgetful).

It’s the thoughtful design that elevates the Backbone One above the rest of the best mobile controllers out there. Slot your phone into the compact cradle, with a USB-C jack for speedy connectivity, and you get satisfyingly clicky and responsive controls plus a 3.5-mm headphone port. You can also customize it for different games, or even use Backbone’s software as a one-stop gaming hub (if you’re willing to pay a subscription).

Recent findings suggest that if you want a virtual screen for gaming that you can take anywhere, the Viture Beast XR are my favorite smart glasses for gaming. These glasses can plug directly into your phone (and many other gadgets) via USB-C to give you a bright 174-inch virtual screen. It's also worth snagging the excellent 8BitDo controller. If these are still too pricey, the Viture Luma Pro for $339 ($160 off) are a good alternative.

Already the cheapest Apple laptop, an extra $50 off the MacBook Neo is not to be sneezed at. In fact, it's a great deal for anyone seeking an affordable laptop that feels premium, with a metal chassis and quality display. The limited 8 GB of RAM is a definite compromise, but for folks with modest needs, the MacBook Neo should serve just fine.

Industry observers note that don't ask me why they keep taking away our ports. God forbid you should want to plug something into your laptop. Well, you can stick it to those minimalist designers with one of the best laptop docks. Despite the small size, this one boasts powerful ports, including 96-watt power delivery and support for up to three 4K displays at a time (or a single 4K monitor at 120 Hz using the USB-C port). The card slots, USB, and headphone jack are up front, with the display, power, and Ethernet ports around back.

The Asus RT-BE58U is perhaps the ideal Wi-Fi 7 upgrade for modest homes and apartments still struggling with the crappy router their internet service provider sent, and that's why it tops our Best Wi-Fi Routers guide. It’s easy to set up and use, can cover up to 2,000 square feet, and has plenty of ports. As a dual-band router, it lacks the 6-GHz band, but it has all the other advantages of Wi-Fi 7. There’s also support for VPN service, separate IoT or guest networks, and Ai Mesh.

We love Amazon's Eero mesh systems for being easy to set up and use, but they also double as smart home hubs with support for Matter, Thread, and Zigbee. The Eero Pro 7 is a tri-band mesh router that adds the 6-GHz band to the familiar 2.4-GHz and 5-GHz bands. For busy households with many devices and a 1-Gbps or faster connection, this mesh system is ideal. Just bear in mind that the 6-GHz band is short-range. The pricey Eero Plus subscription is an extra $10 per month (or $100 per year), but it adds a ton of value with parental controls, advanced security, ad blocking, and even a password manager and VPN service.

Recent findings suggest that this is a rare and tasty deal on my favorite Xmas lights. They work indoors or out, can be scheduled, and support a bunch of lovely animated effects. While I'm on the topic of Philips Hue and its excellent but horribly expensive lights, you might want to check out some of its other Black Friday deals (I would go for the wall washers and the TV lightstrip).

You know what I don't miss? Mowing the lawn. A good robot mower, like this relatively affordable one from TerraMow, will do it for you, quietly. No wire required; it recharges itself. You just set a schedule and relax. OK, it sometimes leaves a verge, but the only model I've tried that doesn't is more than twice the price.

It has been revealed that these wireless noise-canceling headphones may not be the latest release from Sony, but they are still an excellent pair of cans with a far deeper discount. The Sony WH-1000XM5 are relatively light and comfortable, producing accomplished sound in every scenario, and have great control options.

The JBL Flip 7 is the Bluetooth speaker that has it all. It's durable, it has stamina, it produces a punchy sound, and it comes in fun colors. As the best Bluetooth speaker you can buy, this deal is for real.

Yes, you should read more, and Amazon’s Kindle e-readers make it easier to do just that. Our current favorite is the Kindle Paperwhite (12th generation). It has a sharp 7-inch display, auto-adjusting warm light, three-month battery life, and snappy performance, and it’s slim and light. It even has integration with Overdrive for your library books and support for several languages.

In a recent development, our favorite budget Android tablet has a 12.2-inch, 2400 x 1600 pixel LCD panel that’s sharp, colorful, and bright, with a 120-Hz refresh rate. It's perfect for web browsing or kicking back with a movie or sports game, but the aging Qualcomm Snapdragon 4 Gen 2 chipset makes it not the best option for gamers.

Industry observers note that this deal on LG’s 65-inch C6 OLED TV caught my eye. At 48 percent off the regular price, this is the cheapest it has ever been, making it a better option than the entry-level LG B6 we just reviewed. Just make sure you pair it with a streaming device and disable the tracking. There are similar discounts on most of the other sizes of this TV.

Recent findings suggest that released this year, the Samsung S95H OLED TV has never been priced lower than this. This TV promises accurate color and deep blacks. It also sports a snazzy silver bezel that’s recessed behind the main OLED panel that resembles a metal picture frame.

Up your home theater game with a surround sound system from Sony. The Bravia Theater System 6 has a classy, understated design, combining a beefy subwoofer, two tall and musical surround speakers, and a small center soundbar to envelop you in audio. It's a great way to get more from your movies.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, amazon's 12-day holiday shopping marathon has reached the most anticipated day of discounts, Black Friday. The sale began last week, and it's due to run through Cyber Monday on Nov. 30.

Sources indicate that in a organization blog post, Amazon boasted that its holiday savings events would feature "millions of deals across popular categories and upcoming daily themed deal drops," including "double drops" on Black Friday and Cyber Monday proper. Now Black Friday is here; this is what you need to know before you start spending.

Amazon's Black Friday Week sale went live at 3:01 a.m. ET (12:01 a.m. PT) on Nov. 19 — kicking off a full week before Thanksgiving Day. This was the fourth year in a row that Amazon started its Black Friday sale at least a week early.

In a recent development, amazon is hardly the only major retailer to draw out its Black Friday sale. Best Buy, Target, and Walmart have also offered Black Friday deals throughout November — a win for early birds who worry about popular gifts selling out as the holiday shopping season revs up.

Amazon hasn't officially remarked when its 2026 Cyber Monday sale will start, but in the past, it's kicked off the day right after Black Friday. With that in mind, Mashable's Shopping team expects Amazon to make the shift into Cyber Monday mode on Saturday, Nov. 28 this year.

It stands to reason that shoppers want to know which of these days has better deals: Black Friday or Cyber Monday.

Recent findings suggest that it's hard to know whether to take the plunge on the deals today or hang on until Monday. There's no straight answer, as we won't know the deals until they land. But it's worth remembering that Cyber Monday has traditionally been a day for big discounts on electronics and tech. Our advice? If we highlight a deal as a record-low price on Amazon, it's probably worth grabbing it — that price is unlikely to drop much further. Sources indicate that on each day of its Black Friday Week and Cyber Monday sales, Amazon is running themed daily deal drops called "Today’s Significant Deals." These involve limited-time discounts of up to 60% on popular products from brands like Balsam Hill, HydroJug, and Theragun, and they go live once a day except on Black Friday and Cyber Monday proper. Shoppers get two batches of Today's Big Deals on those days: once at 3 a.m. ET, then again at 11 a.m. ET.

Beyond these drops, here are the kinds of Black Friday deals shoppers can expect to see on Amazon:.

Save up to 65% on Amazon's latest gadgets, including the new Alexa Photo Frame, Alexa tablets, Echo Show 16, Echo Time, and Fire TV Stick 4K.

These are some of Amazon's most competitive deals of the year. However, know that its discounts aren't as impressive as they've been on past Black Fridays. That's because myriad products have seen price increases in 2026 due to factors like higher fuel costs, tariffs, and the ongoing memory shortage, aka "RAMageddon.".

The latter is the reason why Amazon raised the prices of its Kindle e-readers, Fire TV Sticks, and most Echo smart speakers in August.

Amazon's Black Friday sale isn't exclusive to Prime members. This is one of the main things that separates it from other Amazon events like Prime Day and Prime Big Deal Days.

Recent findings suggest that no, Amazon does not price-match competitors' deals — not on Black Friday, nor any other day of the year. If you find a better price on something you've recently purchased there, you'll have to return it to Amazon and re-buy it where it's cheaper.

Sources indicate that most items purchased on Amazon from Nov. 1 to Dec. 31 can be returned through Jan. 31, 2026, except for Apple products, which have a return deadline of Jan. 15, 2027.

Sources indicate that if you're in the market for a upcoming screen, now is a smart time to shop options of all sizes, from big, premium OLED TVs for a home theater to small art TVs for the bedroom. Sources indicate that updated November 27: I added WIRED-tested soundbars and projectors on sale from brands like Sonos, Hisense, and XGIMI. I also updated pricing on TV deals.

This is the lowest price I've ever seen the 65-inch LG C6 selling for on Amazon, a fantastic deal on an excellent OLED TV. It's 50 percent off its retail price of $2,700, though it hasn't been sold that high since June. LG's C-Series TVs are consistently among our favorites due to their high brightness, uniform blacks, and vivid, natural colors. Add in their ample connectivity, which makes them versatile enough for gamers, and it's clear why this is a top OLED pick.

The premium 2026 Samsung S95H OLED TV is now at its lowest price yet. WIRED reviewer John Brandon praised the TV for its accurate color and deep blacks. Upcoming to the latest S95H model is a silver bezel that’s recessed behind the main OLED panel, making the TV look like a metal picture frame.

I understand wanting a nice OLED TV but not wanting to pay premium OLED prices. That's where budget OLEDs like the LG B6 shine. Brandon praised the TV's thin size, simple setup, and deep and rich blacks when he tested it last month. It's even more of a standout when it's being discounted this heavily. Just a few days ago, the price had dipped to $1,000, which is a whopping 50 percent off. This was such a good deal, I thought it was a typo at the time. It's since jumped up to $1,200, which is still solid. Pricing is volatile on this one, so I wouldn't be surprised if it drops back to $1,000 at some point over the shopping weekend.

Spoiler for our upcoming review: This is one of the best midrange TVs available. It's a fantastic option that will satisfy most people, and at its current 40-percent-off price, it'll also satisfy most budgets. Like so many of the TVs on the list, this is the lowest price this model has ever dropped to. More importantly, though, WIRED reviewer Rick Broida was seriously impressed by its bright and vibrant color display, which has a distinct pop that’s a joy to behold.

Industry observers note that this isn’t a huge discount at its current price, but the TCL QM6K is one of the best TVs for most people, according to former WIRED reviewer Ryan Waniata. That thanks to its well-rounded picture quality and reasonable price (even when not on sale). I've seen it drop to as low as $528 in the past, so make sure to check back on the price throughout the weekend.

In his review of the Hisense U7SG, Waniata called this a near-premium model with a new-and-improved stand and an anti-reflective matte screen reminiscent of high-end Samsung models. The best part? It's down an extra $50 to its lowest price ever since its launch in April of this year.

In a recent development, the LG Micro RGB Evo takes the top spot in our guide to the best RGB TVs, and again, this is the lowest price I've ever seen for it. WIRED reviewer John Brandon thought movies and demonstrates looked stunning and vivid on its screen, with highly customizable picture settings that put it in a league of its own. Keep in mind that it only comes in 75-, 86-, and 100-inch sizes.

According to recent reports, the best art TV is Samsung's The Frame Pro (2026) thanks to its excellent image quality, contrast, color depth, and anti-glare technology that far outshines the competition, states Brandon. The only problem is that it's historically been high-priced. While 17 percent off may not sound that impressive, it’s actually matching the Prime Day low I saw earlier this year for the same model.

Industry observers note that if you're set on an art TV but can't spring for Samsung's pricey options, this budget-friendly model is the way to go. At 53 percent off, it matches its October Prime Day pricing (which is the lowest it's ever been). It's not as bright as Samsung's art TVs, but it does come with a far broader free art library, no subscription required.

Industry observers note that this is the best soundbar you can get if you want a one-and-done, all-in-one solution. The Sonos Arc Ultra earned high praise from every WIRED reviewer who has tested it (myself included) for it's rich, deep, convincingly spatial sound. If you still want to upgrade, Sonos makes it easy to add other Sonos speakers like a subwoofer or rear surrounds.

This soundbar subwoofer combo is a great way to upgrade your TV audio system with ample bass for a low price, especially with this Black Friday deal. It's simple and easy to use, and doesn't overwhelm with additional features, options, and connectivity like some higher-end options. As log as you don't dream of creating a full surround sound system later, the S4 will serve you for years.

It has been revealed that the Hisense XR10 is an excellent home theater projector thanks to its vivid and sharp color output in movies, TV reveals, and games—it really makes everything pop. At $2,000 off, this is the biggest discount ever for the XR10. Keep in mind, this thing is heavy at 23 pounds, so it's more of a set-it-and-forget-it home projector, and, like many premium projectors, it's only okay when using in a bright, sunny room.

This is the best home theater projector we've tested, and it's at its lowest price to date. Yes, even at 25 percent off, this projector costs a pretty penny, but its dynamic, self-adjusting iris (which automatically increases or reduces light) puts it well above similar competitors. That, plus its outstanding brightness and contrast, means the picture quality is stellar even in broad daylight.

#4566. The British Government is Turning Everyone Into a Prepper

📅 27 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1835 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 WIRED ↗ Open Full Page

The British Government is Turning Everyone Into a Prepper

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1835 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: WIRED

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In 2010, the UK experienced one of its coldest ever winters, with heavy snowfall bringing major roads to a standstill.
  • Next time, Brian decided, he would be prepared.
  • It has been revealed that preppers generally operate on the fringe.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In 2010, the UK experienced one of its coldest ever winters, with heavy snowfall bringing major roads to a standstill. Brian, an engineer in central Scotland, had little food in the house. He donned a backpack, took one of his children’s sledges, and trudged a mile and half to queue outside the nearest supermarket. Shelves were emptying, and tempers were fraying.

Next time, Brian decided, he would be prepared. “It’s very hard to look your kids in the eye when you’re looking at a relatively empty cupboard,” he says. Brian started building up a store of non-perishable food and other supplies, ready for unexpected shortages. He’s now part of the UK’s prepper community—a group of survivalists who blueprint proactively for emergency situations such as natural disasters or infrastructure breakdowns. He shares his tips on YouTube as Scottishprepper73; he reckons his family could live a full year off his stash.

It has been revealed that preppers generally operate on the fringe. They’re used to people considering them crazy and paranoid. When Brian tells friends about his plans, they often respond with jokes. Or worse, they tell him “I’ll just come to your house.” Then, last month, the UK government debuted its “Be Ready” campaign, which advised households to stock up on three days’ worth of bottled water, tinned food, and other essentials. The advice, the Cabinet Office noted, was “the first stage of a three-year campaign to help households across the UK feel better prepared for events such as severe weather, which can occasionally affect services including power, water, phones and the internet.”.

Prepping was flung into the mainstream, and British preppers—a minority in a largely US-dominated scene—have found themselves drawn out of their (metaphorical) bunkers and into the limelight.

For the most part, preppers I spoke to welcomed the government advice, though they unanimously felt it didn't go far enough (“What’s your plan for day four?” Mike Chappell, a Greater Manchester-based prepper, states.) But public reactions, they say, have been mixed.

Industry observers note that dan Goss, who is based in Liverpool and runs the Start Prepping UK website, states traffic to his site “went bananas,” reaching around 50,000 visitors at one point. The news, he says, has “broken people’s normalcy bias,” legitimising the idea of prepping in a way that no amount of bleak climate news can. He’s observed a rise in what he calls the “normal person prepper”—people who aren’t interested in planning for an apocalypse or learning advanced survival skills, but want to build basic household resilience. Glyn Smith, founder of the prepper community UK Survival Network, reports a similar spike in interest. “It’s not lone survivalists; it’s mums, dads, couples, and retirees,” he says. “Normal people who want practical peace of mind.”.

Dan recommends: In terms of hardware or capabilities it’s hard to beat a Sawyer Mini water filter. They’re tiny, lightweight, need no energy source to run, and can filter something like 100,000 liters of water before they need to be replaced.

There’s also been pushback. Every time prepping hits the news, Brian says, some people respond with aggression. When he’s spoken to media before, multiple people have made death threats. “‘I’m not going to waste money on preps, I’ll just buy a shotgun and come to your house,’ yada yada,” he says. For this reason, he, and several other preppers I spoke to, asked to be identified only by their first name. As well as hostility, Goss says, some people complain that they can’t afford to prep, or that the government should provide. A common sentiment, Chappell says, is that “nothing ever happens anyway.” Some accuse preppers of fearmongering.

The general image of the prepping community probably doesn’t help. Think “prepper” and you might imagine a caricature of a man in camo and armed to the teeth, either hunkering down in a nuclear bunker or camping out in the wilderness. But the preppers I speak to present a much more mundane, inclusive, and, well, British approach to prepping. They are keen to distance themselves from the idea of the “doomsday prepper.” Instead, they prep for less extreme but more likely incidents. As the UK anticipates winter weather buffeted by an El Niño climate pattern, they worry about storms, floods, and crop failures. Something as simple as a burst water pipe or power cut could cause localized chaos. Then there’s the threat of cyberattacks: Just this month, supermarket fridges and freezers across Europe were hacked in an attack France believes was conducted by Iran.

Glyn recommends: A Lifesaver bottle or Lifesaver Jerrycan and an EcoFlow power station such as the Delta 3.

It has been revealed that regardless, indicates Ana, a prepper based in south Wales, the impacts are likely to be the same. “It’s going to be affecting potentially your food supply in the supermarkets, your water, your electricity,” she says. Ana has a food channel on YouTube, but pivoted to prepper content when she realized most people had no idea how to preserve food for long-term storage. She grew up growing food, cooking from scratch, and keeping a full pantry, and has maintained these habits. The Covid-19 pandemic reminded her just how vulnerable the UK supply chain is. She was pregnant at the time and noticed a shortage of baby formula; a supermarket worker told her people had been buying it to put in their coffee and tea.

Recent findings suggest that it’s always a good idea to keep a store of basics like bottled water and long-life food. True preppers often invest in more specialized items. Brian gives me a virtual tour of the shed where he stores his supplies, neatly arranged in floor-to-ceiling shelving units. He points to different types of water filtration kits, including a LifeSaver Jerrycan capable of purifying up to 20,000 liters, and rattles off medical supplies (“Antibiotics, tourniquets, chest seals, splints”). He has a few different cooking setups, such as foldable stoves that use gas canisters, and keeps buckets of freeze-dried food that will last for 25 years. Next door, he tells me, there are 165 gallons of fresh water that he refreshes every six months.

In a recent development, brian recommends: A reasonably sized power bank such as a Bluetti Elite 300, which will give you days of backup power for your home. Add in some solar panels and you have a two-to-three-year renewable power source.

According to recent reports, many preppers prepare to go off-grid if the power and internet fail, but Brian has staked his bets on a tech-heavy setup. He has a generator, his house is fitted out with solar panels, and he uses an air source heat pump for heating. He has a backup heater that runs on diesel, and several extremely powerful portable power stations (think a rechargeable power bank, but with enough capacity to keep appliances like a microwave going). He uses Starlink for internet access and runs two different mesh networking systems, with high-frequency radio acting as his ultimate fallback. In his shed, he has plenty of torches, lanterns, candles, radios, walkie-talkies, and a night-vision headset. The way he sees it, you might be able to survive without power, but it wouldn’t be much fun. “We’ve got enough tech these days that life doesn’t have to be uncomfortable,” Brian says.

This is a key difference between the US and UK prepper scenes: While many US preppers initiative to “bug out” and live alone off-grid, British preppers mainly plan to stay at home. “We don’t have that vast wilderness to escape to,” says Chappell, who makes content as the UK Urban Prepper and keeps most of his at-home supplies stacked in what used to be the dining room. When we speak, Chappell has a four-week-old daughter, so his stocks include enough formula milk to get her to solid foods. Nappies are too bulky to stockpile en masse, but he has enough for a short-term concern and a fallback of old-fashioned terry towel nappies.

It has been revealed that mike recommends: My number one would be any kind of water filter. I love the Grayl one for simplicity.

It has been revealed that while prepping is often depicted as a lone wolf activity, British preppers are, on the whole, more community-minded. The scene in general has a degree of secrecy around it; some preppers keep their preps tightly under wraps out of fears that, if people know what they have, they could become a target.

Goss dismisses fears of people turning on each other in a crisis. He evokes a sense of Blitz spirit: when times get tough, he suggests, people tend to come together rather than pull apart. In any case, he doesn’t really have a choice. Like Chappell, he lives in a terraced house in an urban area—a far shout from a private bunker. “Like it or not, you’re going to wind up working with your neighbors during a major giant blackout event or something,” he indicates. “And it would be a really good idea for you to kind of strategy for that ahead of time.” He suggests gaining trust by setting up a street WhatsApp group and doing small favors for neighbors. In an emergency scenario, pooling resources and knowledge may be more effective than going it alone. And if things did descend into looting and fighting–well, wouldn’t you want your neighbors on side?

Recent findings suggest that ana recommends: A power station like Allpowers’ R1500, an Aferiy 2400w station, or the Ecoworthy PS2400. All have great capacity and multiple charging options.

In a recent development, others thought this view might be too optimistic. “When you’re bombarded with information 24/7 and you’re deprived of any information in a general power cut, it wouldn’t take long before people get nervous and start to do stupid things because they panic,” Brian states. “You get a fear response. Fear leads to poor choices, potentially fatal ones.” He’s thought about what he’d do if friends really did turn up on his doorstep like they joke about. “It’s a difficult one,” he says. “I don’t have an answer.”.

It has been revealed that in that kind of scenario, Chappell has a plan to bug out, but just to a family member’s home. His house is surrounded by people he doesn’t know, and he can’t predict how they might react. It’s not that he doesn’t want to help people, he says, but he’s not willing to risk his family’s safety.

Of course, these intends go well beyond a three-day water-and-beans buffer. For many of the people I speak to, prepping is also a hobby. There are meet-ups and workshops. Goss indicates he enjoys camping and tending his allotment—activities that fit neatly into the prepper skillset (he’s also into archery, just to complete the image). But still, it’s nice to be ready, just in case. “This is not a way of life where I sit in a bunker hoping for the sky to fall. I want nothing ever to happen,” Chappell says. “But it’s insurance, right?”.

Scientists Use ‘Grand Theft Auto’ to Model the Effects of Climate Change

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (696 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: WIRED

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • One of the most enticing features of Grand Theft Auto (GTA) is the incredibly well-realized worlds, especially among the most recent installments in the franchise.
  • Developed by Rockstar Games, GTA is one of the most valuable intellectual properties in the video game industry.
  • Sources indicate that like the recently released game—which is so detailed you can even go birding in it—GTA V is a meticulous recreation of the real world.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

One of the most enticing features of Grand Theft Auto (GTA) is the incredibly well-realized worlds, especially among the most recent installments in the franchise. In this detailed rendering, researchers saw an unusual opportunity: What if these video games could be used to model the effects of the climate crisis?

Developed by Rockstar Games, GTA is one of the most valuable intellectual properties in the video game industry. As of this year, the franchise has sold an estimated 465 million units worldwide, and the latest installment in the series, GTA VI, earned $3.79 billion in first-day sales.

Sources indicate that like the recently released game—which is so detailed you can even go birding in it—GTA V is a meticulous recreation of the real world. It’s setting, Los Santos, is a fictional city inspired by Los Angeles and consists of pretty much the same topographical, urban, and coastal features of the Californian metropolis.

These specs were leveraged by Paul Nörenberg, a professor at the University of Potsdam in Germany, and his colleague Hugues Lantuit of the Alfred Wegener Institute, who conducted an experiment to determine whether the video game could serve as a useful tool for projecting the severity and impact of flooding and sea-level rise under various future scenarios related to global warming.

Industry observers note that the authors of the study, published in Geoscience Communication, created a digital model based on the video game’s three-dimensional terrain maps. This allowed them to estimate which areas of Los Santos would be submerged if sea levels continue to rise.

The researchers calculated these possibilities based on two climate scenarios used in the projections of the United Nations Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC).

It has been revealed that the first, known as RCP 2.6, assumes that countries implement effective measures to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and limit global warming. The second, called RCP 8.5, envisions a scenario of high emissions without sufficient mitigation measures. In both cases, the authors made projections of potential climate impacts for the years 2100, 2300, and 2500, and included simulations of storm surges.

Recent findings suggest that the results demonstrated that, in a high-emissions scenario and in the event of a storm surge, sea-level rise and coastal flooding could reach 5.18 meters by 2300. The model estimates that, under these conditions, 5.1 percent of Los Santos’ land area would be flooded, affecting the port, wastewater treatment facilities, and coastal energy infrastructure.

Industry observers note that estimates for the same scenario, but for the year 2500, project that the combined water level would reach 8.22 meters and that 6.5 percent of the land area would be submerged. In contrast, under the emissions-reduction scenario, flooding would affect only 2.2 percent of the territory by 2300, without impacting major infrastructure.

In a second phase, the researchers sought to verify whether the simulations based on the GTA V map could reflect what would happen in the real city. To do so, they compared the results of their model with scientific data on the areas of Los Angeles most vulnerable to flooding. The comparison revealed that the areas identified as vulnerable in the video game coincided with the three locations in the real city most likely to experience flooding: Venice Beach, Pacific Palisades, and the Port of Los Angeles.

“This congruence supports the conclusion that the GTA V terrain is sufficiently faithful to real-world morphology to be scientifically meaningful,” the authors write. The researchers caution, however, that their results should not be interpreted as an exact prediction, since the GTA V model and maps do not account for all possible real-world phenomena that influence flood risk, including wave motion, beach erosion, currents, or changes in terrain.

According to recent reports, the researchers also see a benefit from using GTA V to model climate effects that extends beyond the results themselves. Not only does Los Santos look like the real world, but millions of people have spent countless hours exploring it. For the connection many have to these games, a climate model based in this simulation might feel closer to reality.

This story originally appeared on WIRED en Español and has been translated from Spanish.

Industry observers note that the iPhone 15 Pro models, introduced in 2023, as well as iPhone 16 Pro, had a titanium frame, but Apple went back to aluminum unibody in the iPhone 17 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro. However, the iPhone Air and foldable iPhone Duo still have titanium frames, likely due to the material's lighter weight and better structural strength when compared to aluminum.

The company also uses ceramic parts on some of its devices, notably the Apple Watch Ultra and some variants of the Apple Watch Series 12.

It has been revealed that now, two rumors claim Apple is going to use both these materials in the upcoming iPhone 20 Pro. A leaker called Fixed Focus Digital (via MacRumors) claims that Apple plans to manufacture parts of the phone's mid-frame using 3D-printed titanium. This does not necessarily mean the entire frame will be made of titanium, but it could improve the frame's strength and durability. The Owala FreeSip Stainless Steel Water Bottle (24-Ounce) has earned its viral hype thanks to a smart two-in-one spout that lets you sip upright through a built-in straw or tilt the bottle back to take a big gulp. In Mashable's hands-on testing, Samantha Mangino called it "the water bottle to end all water bottles," noting how the flip-top lid keeps the mouthpiece clean while the carry loop locks it shut so it never leaks in your bag.

Triple-wall insulation keeps ice water cold for up to 24 hours — Mangino even found full ice cubes still clinking around a day later — and the slim base fits easily into standard cup holders and comes apart cleanly for washing.

Sources indicate that the Owala SmoothSip Slider Insulated Coffee Tumbler (20-Ounce) is built to keep hot drinks steaming for up to 6 hours and iced coffees chilled for up to 24 hours without spilling in your bag. Its smooth slider spout delivers a comfortable sip while sealing shut to prevent splashes and leaks on bumpy morning commutes. It is also BPA- and phthalate-free and features a dishwasher-safe lid for quick cleanup.

The Owala FreeSip Sway Stainless Steel Water Bottle (30-Ounce) gives you more capacity without forcing you to give up your car's cup holder, thanks to a tapered base that fits in most standard cup holders. Like the classic FreeSip, its push-button lid flips open to reveal a two-in-one spout for sipping upright through a built-in straw or tilting back for a bigger gulp, while a sliding lock keeps it 100 percent leakproof in your bag.

It also swaps the standard carry loop for a comfortable top bucket handle, keeps cold drinks chilled for up to 24 hours with triple-wall insulation, and features a wide mouth for easy ice loading and cleaning.

Retire that dented, sticker-covered bottle sitting on your desk and grab a fresh Owala while the Black Friday markdowns are still flowing.

With the weather worsening, taking advantage of Black Friday toy deals and picking up discounted board games or Lego sets could be a very smart move. The WIRED Reviews team has a bunch of kids of all ages between us, and most of us are still big kids at heart, so we’ve tried a lot of board games and toys over the years.

Recent findings suggest that the best Black Friday deals are well and truly on, and that includes some of the best family board games, best STEM toys, and best gifts for Lego lovers. I have handpicked a selection of WIRED-tested and approved options for you right here, so whether you’re buying gifts or just treating yourself, there’s sure to be something to put a smile on your face.

In a recent development, what kid doesn’t love a marble run? This clever release from ThinkFun combines the fun of dropping marbles with logic puzzles that challenge kids to build a 3D maze that can guide the marble to the target end spot by building connected towers. It’s one of the best STEM toys we’ve tried, and it goes down a storm with most kids aged eight years and up.

Recent findings suggest that this irresistible construction kit from our best STEM toys guide is a wonderful gift for kids of all ages. Clixo’s colorful, versatile magnetic pieces snap together, letting you build all kinds of three-dimensional shapes, from crowns to cats. The pieces stack neatly and are very compact when packed away. Clixo sets are also durable and washable, and you can play with them anywhere. Clixo kits are suitable for kids aged 4 and up.

Sources indicate that the tough, translucent Magna-Tiles click together easily to form two-dimensional shapes and three-dimensional objects. Kids love building houses, castles, vehicles, and whatever else they can imagine with these triangular and square magnetic tiles. The classic set is a great start, but be warned: There are themed sets, and you will end up buying more! I recommend the Undersea Adventure set.

This Bluetooth-enabled chess board connects to an app on your phone, and you can play against remote players or yourself, or get AI coaching to improve your game. You can scale the assistance you want, with different-colored lights that advise you of moves as you pick up each piece. It’s perfect for beginners and kids. Particula also makes a Harry Potter-themed version that appears in our best smart chess boards guide.

Azul is about making mosaics by matching tiles with different patterns and colors to get the maximum possible score. It’s easy to grasp but supports many different tactical approaches and has surprising depth. The tiles and other components are high quality, and filling your board is deeply satisfying. Play moves quickly, and you can complete a game in less than an hour, but you will want to play again.

Industry observers note that this beautifully themed game casts players as villains from the Star Wars universe, such as Darth Vader and Moff Gideon. If you’ve played other games in the Villainous series, you’ll know every character gets a unique set of victory conditions, and you can meddle with the other player’s attempts to win. There’s a definite learning curve, and some characters are easier to win with than others. This game is best for four players aged 10 years and up.

In a recent development, this immersive strategy game is all about gathering and trading resources to build roads, settlements, and cities on a randomly generated board of hexagonal tiles. Collecting enough points to win requires the right strategy and a bit of luck with dice rolls. My kids love the trading and the robber mechanic, which allows you to steal cards from your opponents and block their resources (though it can cause arguments). The game is perfect for three or four players and usually lasts around an hour.

Industry observers note that the perfect spooky board game for classic horror fans, you must work cooperatively to defeat old horror-movie monsters like Dracula, the Wolf Man, and the Mummy. Cooperative games are perfect for family board game night, and this one is challenging enough that you really have to communicate well and work together if you want to avoid an untimely death and save the townsfolk.

Some of the best family board games are cooperative, so you can avoid those arguments that sometimes lead to board flipping and huffs, and Pandemic is a solid example. There’s a worldwide pandemic, and you must work together for the survival of mankind by jetting around the board and trying to halt the spread. Each player assumes a role, like a scientist or medic, with unique special powers, and you must strategize and coordinate to emerge alive.

This Lego set is perfect for a table or shelf once built; you can put the roses in a vase. You get a combination of 4 roses in full bloom, 4 blossoming roses, and 4 rosebuds, each with stems, along with 4 sprigs of white baby's breath flowers. There are three sets of instructions for building with family or friends, and this Lego set makes a great quirky gift. You can also get the Lego Botanicals Mini Bonsai Trees for $45 right now ($20 off).

In a recent development, this fun parody throws the best of Batman’s movies into a blender with slapstick comedy and plenty of charm. You’ll scour Gotham for collectibles, uncover puzzles to solve, and face off against an army of thugs and villains. Melee combat is fun, as you counter and dodge to build combos, with a selection of classic gadgets at your disposal. This is the best Lego video game in recent years, and it’s perfect for split-screen couch co-op.

Best Kitchen Gifts for Home Cooks (2026)

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that I’ve been cooking dinner for myself (and/or my family) nearly every night for the past 27 years.
  • Sources indicate that some of my favorite kitchen gadgets may not be the most flashy (a measuring cup, a mesh cloth, a cast-iron pan).
  • I've also thrown in a couple of fun nice-to-haves, including a kit for making Giada De Laurentiis' viral (and highly recommended!) sheet-pan lasagna and a 500-piece puzzle that may send you on a soup-making side quest.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that I’ve been cooking dinner for myself (and/or my family) nearly every night for the past 27 years. Suffice it to say I've learned some kitchen tips and tricks during those decades—especially about what is and isn't worth taking up valuable counter space.

Sources indicate that some of my favorite kitchen gadgets may not be the most flashy (a measuring cup, a mesh cloth, a cast-iron pan). Instead, they're the kinds of things that really matter when you cook a lot, whether in service of keeping things clean and organized, or sharp, or preserving your hard work by freezing leftovers for a future busy night.

I've also thrown in a couple of fun nice-to-haves, including a kit for making Giada De Laurentiis' viral (and highly recommended!) sheet-pan lasagna and a 500-piece puzzle that may send you on a soup-making side quest.

For more gift ideas, check out our Best Gifts Under $100, Best Tech Gifts, and Best Gifts Under $25.

In a recent development, if your giftee loves baking sourdough but hates having to feed their starter every day or revive it every time it goes in the fridge, this could be a game-changing device—it was for me. It requires some futzy calibration and adjustment at first, but I've kept my starter going and in a ready-to-use state for almost a month with this handy gadget that works for any type of flour.

Cast iron cookware is unparalleled for its heat retention, durability, and nonstick nature, so long as you keep it well seasoned. But it's also heavy and often difficult to maneuver. You could always use lightweight carbon steel, made with an iron-carbon alloy, but it doesn't really act like cast iron in that it's highly variable in terms of heat. Field's heirloom-quality pans are modeled on smooth vintage designs and are just as lightweight as stainless steel, yet retain all the benefits of cast iron. WIRED operations manager Scott Gilberston likes them a lot, and so do I.

Industry observers note that even though I cook every day, I'm terrible at sharpening knives. I never feel like I'm doing it correctly on the manual honing rods or pull-through sharpeners, but with this electric model, I found success. There's still a learning curve, but once you get the hang of it, you'll be able to sharpen a whole block's worth of knives in about half an hour. I was even able to revive a chef's knife that hadn't been sharpened in nearly 20 years, sitting dull and forgotten at the back of a drawer.

After I lived in Mexico for a year, I became unable to eat store-bought tortillas. Sure, they're easy, with no preparation required beyond warming them. But they're also limp, flavorless, sad little excuses for food. Alternatively, homemade tortillas are things of beauty and exemplify what I love about cooking: using simple, high-quality ingredients to produce something far better than you would expect. Fortunately, making your own tortillas is incredibly easy—well, if you have a tortilla press, and the best I've used is this one from Masienda, which nicely offers the ability to press larger tortillas.

Sources indicate that if your foodie friend likes Mexican food, this gift will expand their culinary horizons. The combo pack provides everything they need to get started on making their own tortillas: masa and a press. The key to great homemade tortillas is great masa harina, and Masienda's flour is my favorite (well, outside of Mexico anyway). —Scott Gilbertson.

Industry observers note that look, we’re big fans at WIRED of the viral (and manly) Männkitchen pepper mill and its 50 grind settings, but its plain black basic-peppermill look isn’t exactly giftable. HexMill's HexClad burr-grinder pepper mill is pretty darn close in terms of performance, with 10 grind settings and a lifetime warranty. Plus, it comes in four anodized aluminum colors that make it feel special and personalized. I also like that it holds up to half a cup of peppercorns—more than any other pepper mill I've tried. I've been using one of these almost daily for the past few months and haven't had to refill it yet.

Who doesn't love a quick and easy sheet-pan meal? If you haven’t yet tried making Giada De Laurentiis’ viral sheet-pan lasagna, you should. This kit allows your giftee to make it just as the celebrity chef intended, with purée made from hand-picked tomatoes in Salerno, Italy; organic olive oil from Coratina; a custom salt blend; and a box of taccole cut in Abruzzo on 100-year-old bronze dies.

In a recent development, you'll need to buy the perishables, like ricotta, sausage, and vegetables. But the recipe is worth the extra spend, considering how much food the kit makes; the description indicates six servings, but it could easily feed double that if you throw in a side salad. Note that the included recipe is a bit vague on equipment, but to prepare the sausage and onions, you'll need a 14-inch pan; my 12-incher was not major enough.

This gift is a great mix of beauty and utility. Many of my cook friends already have serious affection for All-Clad's set of measuring spoons ($35), which are preciously shaped not like spoons but like miniature All-Clad pans—a visual pun that also makes small measures of spices or flour much easier to parse visually than you could with a spoon-shaped spoon.

This set is even more special—and useful. It includes the odd and vexing sizes that nonetheless turn up constantly in baking recipes: 1.5 teaspoons or 1.5 cups, a ¾ cup or a ⅔ cup. These are measurements that often require eyeballing or using multiple measuring cups to achieve. Any cook, and especially any baker, who receives this gift will feel both charmed and understood. —Matthew Korfhage.

It has been revealed that even before the advent of the Gen Z aesthetic police (no offense; I live with one) and ASMR “restock my pantry” reels, there's been something irresistible about a perfectly organized set of spices. Evermill's has been popular for a while, and for good reason—there's no kitchen where this sleek black (or white, silver, or gunmetal) rack wouldn't look good.

And these aren't your typical spice jars prefilled with dusty, flavorless grounds, either. You'll get to pick which ones you want, and they're fresh and organic and come in resealable bags so you can add as much or as little as you want at a time.

According to recent reports, as former WIRED reviewer Matthew Korfhage has stated, “Every cook has seen these checkerboard-looking cutting boards and thirsted for them a little.” No lies detected. The handsome look comes from end-grain pieces for a more durable surface. It's a hefty board that's intended to be out in your kitchen full time, not tucked away in a cabinet. Korfhage had the walnut version, but I have the maple version, which is a little cheaper but still showstopping.

Thirty-five Southeast Asian noodle dishes—including pho, bun bo hue, noodle plates, fish ball soups, and more—form a colorful mosaic in this 500-piece puzzle. Visual artist and world traveler Troy Litten photographed (and ate!) all the plates featured. It's a fun gift for any puzzle-loving foodie or world traveler you know. I lent it to two people who tend to prefer puzzles of at least 1,000 pieces, and they still loved this one, finding it challenging enough to hold their interest.

According to recent reports, A vacuum sealer has always been one of my most-used kitchen appliances, for both sous vide cooking and sealing large-batch leftovers. The vacuum sealer I owned, a FoodSaver, was massive and cost more than $200 at the time. This Fresko model is small enough to fit in a cabinet (roughly 16 inches long by 8 inches wide) and also comes with a roll of food-safe, cut-to-fit bags and 10 pre-cut bags that are perfect for most items. I've used the Fresko for both wet goods like marinated meats, and dry like frozen blocks of sauces and leftovers (made with Souper Cubes, below). No matter the item, I've never had any complications getting a good seal.

Instant-read thermometers are something every cook should have. It might be cool to saunter over to the grill and gently prod your steak with a finger and pronounce it medium well, but few of us can reliably do that. The Thermapen One will tell you the exact internal temperature in one second. No need for elaborate guesswork.

It has been revealed that cheap instant-read thermometers litter Amazon, but we like the more expensive Thermapen One for its reliability (mine is five years old and still going strong) and speed. Yes, speed really does matter, because the longer the oven is open or the grill lid is off, the more it cools and the more unevenly you end up cooking. Get them the best thermometer, and you'll guarantee they'll temp your hanger steak exactly the way you like it. —Scott Gilbertson.

Many cooks put a lot of time and effort into making not only meals but things that make the meals—stocks, broths, sauces, chopped vegetables, beans. I have been obsessed with Souper Cubes for years, as they allow me to freeze my hard work for later, as well as preserve about-to-go-bad store-bought sauces, salsas, and even tomato paste in specific increments like half-cups, tablespoons, or even one- or two-cup blocks. I then like to vacuum seal them, but you can also just put the cubes in a zip-lock bag. There are cheaper versions of these out there, but Souper Cubes have steel wire inside so they won't crush, sag, or crumple, plus their lids let you stack them in the freezer.

If you’re a baker, especially of long doughs like pizza and bread, you’re likely all too familiar with the difficulty of cleaning bowls, mixers, starter containers, and any other surface that touched sticky, developed gluten. It doesn’t take much for sponges—or sinks, or pipes—to become entombed in the stuff, sometimes intractably. The answer is the Keeki Cloth, a square of webbed polyester mesh that cleans even the biggest baking messes effectively and immediately. Best of all, it’s machine washable, so you can thoroughly clean and sanitize it before its next use.

It has been revealed that I’ve been using—and machine-washing—mine for over a year, and it still looks good as fresh. In fact, I love it so much, I often use it with dish soap to clean regular dishes of stuck-on food. A three-pack is just $15, making it an easy stocking stuffer, hostess gift, or reason to keep a few in rotation.

Aarke's Carbonator 3 lives full-time on my kitchen counter, mainly for cocktails and making my own sparkling-water concoctions. But adding sparkling water to batter for tempura and waffles is a known hack to make them lighter and crispier, so the machine could also double as a chef's tool. I also appreciate that it uses no electricity, so you don't need to situate it near an outlet. This retro appliance is a showpiece in any color option, but Aarke gilded the lily with a newly introduced line of vintage-inspired shades this year, including textured Heritage Green (shown) and Burgundy.

No herb garden in December? No problem. I keep herbs in my kitchen year-round thanks to the Auk, which is one of the most thoughtfully designed indoor hydroponic garden setups I've ever used. It comes with parsley and basil seeds, but you can grow anything you want in the coco coir pots, as well as adjust light schedules and initiate vacation mode (which dims the lights for slower growth) in the easy-to-use app. The mid-century-inspired Scandinavian design is a bonus.

It has been revealed that turn the downside of cooking—doing dishes—into an upside with a thoughtfully designed dish rack. I know few people with a truly functional dish rack situation, and this is the best one I have ever owned. It's got a little tower for wine glasses and a tray for small items like gaskets and caps. The best part may just be the bottom that slopes into a spout that drains right back into the sink. No more moldy, wet drying mats or water dripping onto the floor.

Sources indicate that I use steak knives for a lot more than meat—bread, produce, cutting sandwiches in half, even opening packages in a pinch—which means my steak knives often end up in rough shape, making for a sad complement on the table when I actually do make steaks for company or even just my family. A set of “good” steak knives is something your cooking giftee may not bother buying for themself, but I highly recommend having it. This Anolon set is my favorite, as there are no plastic or wooden handles to weather or discolor, and the knives have a good weight to them.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, there’s no denying that 2026 has been a slower year for the iPad lineup.
  • With the best Black Friday deals flowing, solid markdowns make now a smart time to shop for an iPad.
  • I was delighted to see that Apple’s brand-new iPad Mini is already on sale—especially for this much.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, there’s no denying that 2026 has been a slower year for the iPad lineup. Only the iPad Air and iPad Mini received updates (with nothing latest for the iPad or iPad Pro since 2025), and in June, the entire lineup saw a painful price hike of $100 or $200, depending on the model. But that doesn’t mean you have to abandon your dreams of getting a great deal on a great iPad this year. The best Black Friday iPad deals could be exactly what you've been waiting for.

With the best Black Friday deals flowing, solid markdowns make now a smart time to shop for an iPad. For more shopping advice from our team of product testers and deal hunters, check out our Best Amazon Black Friday Deals, Best Black Friday MacBook Deals, and Best Black Friday Laptop Deals.

I was delighted to see that Apple’s brand-new iPad Mini is already on sale—especially for this much. There’s a lot I loved about the latest iPad Mini, which comes with the A20 Pro chip and an OLED screen, but the price was a tough pill to swallow. But for $100 off, it feels completely worth the money. It’s better than the previous model in every way, with a thinner tablet, a slightly larger screen, and a front-facing camera moved to landscape for better video calls.

Recent findings suggest that if you’re trying to save the most cash, the base iPad is the absolute cheapest. You might also appreciate the larger screen over the iPad Mini. The standard $50 discount has been upped to $70 off for Black Friday, which makes it a great time to buy the base iPad. It’s particularly attractive if you need something for an upcoming flight or to keep kids busy on a long holiday road trip.

Recent findings suggest that the iPad Air is the in-between iPad. It’s not as cheap as the base iPad, nor does it have the Tandem OLED screen and high-end features of the iPad Pro. And yet, I think it’s the iPad people should buy if they strategy to use it for work. That’s mainly because it has a powerful M4 chip and can connect to a Magic Keyboard with full trackpad support. The most recent versions of iPadOS make windowing much easier, and Apple even made the cursor work more like macOS. After all, most people don’t need an OLED screen for word processing, answering emails, and the occasional Zoom call.

When you’re ready to use it more like a traditional tablet, just pull it off its magnetic cover, and it’s ready for your fingers or an Apple Pencil. The 11-inch model is still small enough to not feel overwhelming in your hands. And while the $649 sale isn’t particularly rare, it’s not a bad price for a tablet that works well as a laptop replacement.

iPad Pro 11-inch for $1,049: It’s surprising that the iPad Pro hasn’t been heavily discounted at all for Black Friday. At $1,049, it’s cheaper than the 13-inch MacBook Air, which uses the same M5 chip. The difference? You still have to buy the Magic Keyboard separately to pair with the iPad Pro. All in all, the iPad ends up being much more expensive.

It has been revealed that iPad Mini (2024) for $499: Like the newer iPad Mini, the 2024 model is also $100 off. The upgrades in the 2026 model are worth the money, but if you just need something simple to take notes or read books on, this previous model will do the trick.

iPad Pro 13-Inch for $1,697: The 13-inch iPad Pro has been fluctuating in price since we started monitoring Black Friday sales. At one point, it was as low as $1,349—a terrific deal for Apple’s flagship iPad. It is a bit of a niche tablet because of the price alone, but if you want an iPad that can properly replace a high-end laptop, the 13-inch model is substantial enough (and fast enough) for the job. The sale has ended since we last checked, but we’re keeping it on our list—it’s worth checking in case it goes on sale again.

The third-generation Kindle Scribe is down to $350 from $500, making it cheaper to buy than the $400 second-gen version. Looking to escape the Kindle ecosystem, or want your first e-reader to be Amazon-free? The Kobo Libra Colour is both the model and Black Friday deal for you. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • In 2026, Black Friday is a marathon, not a sprint.
  • Not too long ago, if you wanted to score Black Friday deals, you either had to head to your local Target at the crack of dawn or line up just after Thanksgiving dinner leftovers had been packed away.
  • These days, Black Friday sales start as early as October and stretch for weeks before the actual day arrives, which raises a very real question: Is Cyber Monday still a thing?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In 2026, Black Friday is a marathon, not a sprint. The only thing is, these days it can be hard to tell where the starting line — or the finish line — actually is. With Amazon's Black Friday Week sale running since Nov. 19 and Cyber Monday right around the corner on Nov. 30, plenty of major markdowns are already live.

Not too long ago, if you wanted to score Black Friday deals, you either had to head to your local Target at the crack of dawn or line up just after Thanksgiving dinner leftovers had been packed away. Online shoppers bided their time until the Monday after the holiday, a day eventually dubbed Cyber Monday. It was chaos, sure, but it had clearly defined time parameters.

These days, Black Friday sales start as early as October and stretch for weeks before the actual day arrives, which raises a very real question: Is Cyber Monday still a thing? And for an online-only retailer like Amazon, where most folks do their holiday shopping, is it better to buy today on Black Friday or wait until Cyber Monday on Nov. 30 to score the best deals?

Here's what our shopping spidey-sense, based on many collective years of covering these sales, leads us to believe.

In our experience, Black Friday deals at Amazon tend to be better and more plentiful than Cyber Monday savings, though they can be on par. In the years we've worked this sale, we've very rarely seen additional price cuts or brand-newly introduced deals crop up for Cyber Monday. While Amazon does hold back a handful of fresh drops for Monday — including scheduled twice-daily deal drops at midnight and 8 a.m. PT — those additions tend to be smaller in scope and rarely beat Black Friday pricing on major tech from brands like Apple, Samsung, Sony, Ninja, and Nintendo.

Recent findings suggest that now that the holiday shopping season begins so early, Black Friday has started to feel like the grand finale, with Cyber Monday like an encore. Over the past week, we have already seen flagship gadgets hit record-low prices ahead of and during Black Friday, including $149 Apple AirPods Pro 3, $299 Apple Watch Series 12 models, and $348 Sony WH-1000XM6 headphones.
